smells.finding: identify_straight_arcs body is ~15 lines; bin_row_to_descriptor and descriptors_from_frame are each under 15 lines. No method grew unwieldy.
Only frozen value-object dataclasses (BrakingArc, StraightArc) with 3-4 scalar fields each; no behavior-bearing class.

The gate's central requirement -- _contiguous_runs is the single grouping implementation, called by both identify_braking_arcs({_BRAKE_REGIME}) and identify_straight_arcs(_STRAIGHT_REGIMES); grep confirms no second copy exists anywhere in the repo. Both identify_* functions share the loop-over-runs-build-dataclass idiom but compute materially different per-run fields (peak_decel/mean_speed/quantile-filter vs length_m/duration_s/top_speed_ms) -- this is shared idiom, not duplicated logic.
Each new function operates only on its own declared inputs (samples/run indices, or mu_lat_p90/v_mean/df); no reaching into unrelated objects' internals.

bin_row_to_descriptor's (mu_lat_p90, v_mean) pair is 2 primitives always used together, but 2 args is below the threshold worth a parameter object, and descriptors_from_frame already provides the batched/frame-shaped entry point for the N-row case.
bin_row_to_descriptor returns tuple[float, float] rather than a NamedTuple/dataclass for (radius_m, lateral_g); a named type would self-document the two fields.

override.repo_standard: Existing repo precedent in the same subsystem: src/physics/layer2/damage_candidates.py's lateral_kinematics (imported and used by grip_bin_obs.py, the direct upstream of this new module) already returns a bare tuple (speed, a_long, a_lat, dt) for a small multi-value pure-function result -- and the handoff's own close criteria specify this exact signature (bin_row_to_descriptor(mu_lat_p90: float, v_mean: float) -> tuple[float, float]) byte-for-byte.
override.reason: Plain-tuple multi-return for small kinematic/physics conversion functions is an established local convention in src/physics/layer2 (not just this handoff's ask), so a bare tuple here is consistent with the surrounding module family rather than a one-off shortcut.

smells.finding: Max parameter count in any changed/new function is 3 (samples, min_len, regimes); well within norm.

Generalizing _contiguous_runs required touching exactly its one definition plus its one existing caller (identify_braking_arcs) to pass the now-required regimes arg; the new caller (identify_straight_arcs) is additive. No scattered multi-file edit was needed for one concept.

arcs.py now hosts two arc families, but they are the designed, named Phase-1 deliverable pairing (braking + straight) sharing one factored grouping core -- this is the intended module boundary (struct:physics.layer2), not an accidental grab-bag accreting unrelated reasons to change.
No deep attribute-chain traversals; samples[i].position / .speed / .timestamp_ms are single-hop attribute reads on the same KinematicSample-shaped object throughout.

_contiguous_runs's regimes: set[str] generalization has two real, immediately-used callers (identify_braking_arcs and identify_straight_arcs) in this same diff -- satisfies the 'two adapters make a seam real' bar, not a hypothetical extension point built for nobody.

Docstrings explain physical formulas (a_lat = v^2/R) and design provenance (why _STRAIGHT_REGIMES is derived, not re-listed); the underlying code is already clear without them -- comments add domain context, they do not compensate for confusing code.
